item.title: 'SNL' host Michael Che mocks Macklemore's 'Free Palestine tour' after Ed Sheeran drops rapper
item.description: Michael Che mocked Macklemore's "Free Palestine Tour" on "Weekend Update" after the rapper was dropped from Ed Sheeran's U.S. stadium concerts.
item.content:encoded:
"Saturday Night Live" comedian Michael Che mocked rapper Macklemore during "Weekend Update" on Saturday night in New York City over his newly announced "Free Palestine Tour," which came after the rapper was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. stadium tour following his pro-Palestinian performances earlier this month.

Che set up the joke by noting Macklemore’s removal from Sheeran’s tour before turning to the rapper’s new slate of concerts.

"Rapper Macklemore, who was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran, announced that he is launching a Free Palestine tour," Che said. 

"But haven’t the Palestinian people been through enough?" he asked. 

BILL MAHER HAMMERS MACKLEMORE OVER GAZA REMARKS, HIGHLIGHTS RAPPER'S CONTROVERSIAL 'JEW' COSTUME FROM 2014

Christian Toto, an award-winning film critic, journalist and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital that celebrity commentary about the Israel-Palestinian conflict often follows what he described as a socially rewarded position within the entertainment industry.

"There is only one acceptable answer for celebrities when it comes to the ongoing Israel/Palestinian conflict. Say 'Free Palestine' and nothing else. It's the new BLM, a contentious issue where celebrities know they'll gain approval within their circle by repeating that mantra. They also understand they won't be pressured to defend their point of view by the vast majority of entertainment reporters. It's a safe space for them," Toto said.

"Journalists now know they can pepper stars with similar questions and get a similar response (and lots of clicks for their interviews)," he continued.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

Macklemore announced the "Free Palestine Tour" on Thursday, with shows scheduled for Dublin on Oct. 26, Paris on Oct. 29 and London on Oct. 30. Additional performers and U.S. dates were expected to be announced later, while proceeds will benefit organizations supporting Palestinians, according to the rapper.

In announcing the tour, Macklemore argued that artists could no longer remain outside the debate over the war in Gaza.

"It’s 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn’t work anymore," Macklemore said. "People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it."

MS RACHEL URGES 'EVERY WEALTHY WHITE CELEBRITY' TO MATCH MACKLEMORE'S DONATION TO PALESTINIAN CAUSES

The announcement followed weeks of controversy after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his protest song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4 and 5. 

The Messina Touring Group said multiple upcoming venues would not permit concerts to take place with Macklemore on the lineup.

Sheeran later stressed that he was not personally responsible for removing Macklemore and said he had attempted to resolve the dispute before the venues and promoter made their decision. 

Fox News Digital reported that Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga subsequently withdrew from Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

"Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine," Sheeran said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Macklemore said he would donate the $1 million he earned from Sheeran's tour to organizations providing aid to Palestinians. Sheeran and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft also announced plans for $2 million contributions toward humanitarian relief in the region.

When asked whether increasingly political performances risk turning entertainment into a litmus test for performers and audiences, Toto said he believes most musicians remain cautious about alienating concertgoers.

"Most artists know better than to alienate audiences with their political views. The Springsteens, Morellos and Macklemores remain the exception. Concert ticket prices are too high for most bands to get on their soapbox and risk dooming repeat business," Toto told Fox News Digital. "Actors don't make the connection between their divisive words and audience reaction. They simply want to appease their fellow actors and make nice with potential directors and casting directors. So they read from the approved script."

Fox News Digital reached out to Kraft, Sheeran and Macklemore for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Rod Stewart confirms final tour after heart procedure and health scares
item.description: Rod Stewart announced his "Final Encore Tour," revealing next year's dates will be his last-ever tour after a coronary stent procedure and health setbacks.
item.content:encoded:
Rod Stewart is ready for one final encore.

The rock legend announced "The Final Encore Tour" Monday, revealing that next year will mark his last-ever tour after facing a series of health issues.

"Well, here we go… one last time!" Stewart wrote on Instagram. "Come and see me on my The Final Encore Tour for one more round of rock ’n’ roll. I’m really looking forward to it."

ROD STEWART CALLED 'TONE-DEAF' FOR ATTENDING WORLD CUP GAME A DAY CANCELING CONCERT DUE TO HEALTH ISSUES

Stewart opened up about his decision to make the tour his last in an emotional video message.

"Ladies and gentlemen, after much deliberation and sadness, I have to announce next year will be my last tour ever, ever, ever," he told fans.

"I’m not retiring, but this will be the last rock and roll tour," he clarified.

"I wanna thank you for everything you’ve given me, and hopefully I’ve given you something in return," Stewart said before singing, "Please come out and see me on the tour. It’s gonna be great!"

In the comments, fans said they were "heartbroken" and thanked Stewart for his music.

"Sir Rod, After 53 years and nearly 300 shows across four continents, I am heartbroken that I just have one more year of your AMAZING live shows. Can’t wait to see ALL of them. Thank you for a lifetime of music that created incredible moments and memories. You live will be missed," one fan wrote.

"You have given me so much joy, a real good reason to travel the world and the chance to met wonderful people (some of whom I can call my friends now). Gratitude, Respect and Love forever," another wrote.

Another fan added, "Love you Sir Rod!! Thank you for all the Rock N Roll you given all of us!!" 

"You have given us so much there are no words. Wishing you all the very best," one fan wrote.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Stewart has faced a string of health setbacks in recent years.

He has canceled shows after battling strep throat, COVID-19 and the flu.

His health troubles continued in 2026, when a sinus infection and an acute upper respiratory infection that led to laryngitis forced additional cancellations. 

In August, Stewart canceled the remaining dates of his "One Last Time Tour" after undergoing a coronary stent procedure.

"Doctors are pleased with his recovery, and Rod is doing very well and has returned to his normal daily activities," Stewart's team shared on Instagram at the time. "On the advice of his doctors, he will take the next four weeks to recuperate and regain full fitness before returning to the stage."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Stewart's wife, Penny Lancaster, later explained why doctors recommended that the singer take a break from touring to recover from his heart procedure, describing his intense routine.

"So, he’s on the cycling machine warming his legs up, he’s warming his voice up, he’s getting prepared with his outfit, it’s like pumping his chest, you know? And he comes out the dressing room, and it’s that walk down the corridor to his stage," she said during an appearance on the "At Home with Vanessa" podcast. "And once he gets onstage, he doesn’t just walk on, like he runs on. And the first song, it’s like go, go, go. And he does that for like an hour and a half, two hours."

Lancaster said Stewart's demanding routine was why doctors wanted him to give his body time to heal.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"So of course, [the] doctor’s recommendation was not touring, not doing those shows for four weeks to have a full recovery so that he is fit to go back. But he’s already back in the gym," she shared on the podcast.

Lancaster admitted that keeping the energetic rocker from overdoing it had become a team effort.

"Between me and my brother, his trainer, and doctors and everyone, you know, we’re not letting him get away with it ... he has to do as he’s told," she revealed about the singer's recovery.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: Senate Republicans scrap early exit from Washington as midterm stakes soar
item.description: Senate Republicans force a test vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act, daring Democrats to block a data center affordability bill boosting Jon Husted.
item.content:encoded:
It’s a calculation by Republicans to keep the Senate in session this week.

Yes. The Senate was scheduled to meet anyway over the next few days. But the general consensus early last week was that the Senate would be done then, and those facing competitive races would be back home campaigning.

Then Wednesday hit.

Republicans wanted to stay in Washington. For a very specific reason. And many of them told Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., as much at their weekly luncheon.

"Odds are we plan on being here next week," said Thune.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS STRUGGLES TO FIND A MESSAGE THAT RESONATES WITH VOTERS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

One Senate aide compared the Senate’s schedule to a cat chasing a beam of light from a laser pointer.

But the Senate is in fact meeting. There are reasons. Most of them are political.

The Senate wasn’t quite done with the bill to regulate money in intercollegiate athletics last week. And with the affordability question vexing Republicans, they really didn’t want to pass the college sports bill and promptly vacate Washington. That would be an awkward punctuation point at the end of the legislative sentence before the midterms. GOPers wanted something more substantive. Democrats might have presented that opportunity to Republicans on a platter.

Before the House left for the midterms the week before last, it accentuated its session by passing the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. Let me tell you, not much passes around here with 417 votes. Like their Senate colleagues, House Republicans also worry about voters doubting they’re addressing affordability. So this bill hit the mark for them.

The legislation defrays the costs ratepayers fork out for their utility bills if they’re driven up by data centers. This forces the tech companies which run the data centers to foot the bill.

Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is one of the most vulnerable Republicans on the ballot this fall. Husted’s longtime support for data centers is also dragging him down in the eyes of some voters. Husted tried to fix that. He went to the floor and asked for the Senate to pass on the spot the House bill. However, Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., objected, blocking the effort.

FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE

Republicans viewed that as an opening. Democrats stood in the way of passing a bill on affordability which 417 bipartisan House members supported without blinking. Senate GOPers immediately seized this opportunity as a wedge against their adversaries. And, they interpreted this as a chance to assist their Ohio colleague.

"Tell the data centers we're happy to have you. But you've got to pay your own electricity. People are not going to pay for it," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.

Republicans were already leery about the uneven political footing when it comes to AI. Even more so with data centers. Voters are not enamored with the results of the Big, Beautiful Bill, passed last summer. But dealing with data centers is more immediate and might resonate with those who soured on the Republican brand.

"In Missouri, people are absolutely scared to death that these data centers are going to take all the prime farm ground of the state. And then they're going to raise electricity bills so high, no one will be able to afford them," said Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo.

The official schedule intended for the Senate to meet this week. But once September hit and no government shutdown loomed, senators from both sides – especially those facing challenging elections – wanted to skip Washington and campaign back home. Yours truly asked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., why his party stood in the way of the Senate aligning with the House on that data center/utilities measure.

"Was this blocked in the Senate last week by Democrats as an effort to prevent Sen. Husted from having a win in this competitive race?" I asked.

"Sen. Husted's bill is a fraud. It's voluntary. No company has to do it. The bill we have is mandatory. It is much stronger and is what is needed," replied Schumer.

There is something to Schumer’s argument about how muscular the bill is. The legislation says public utility regulators must only consider a standard for ratepayers. Nothing is required. Thus, there’s wiggle room for tech firms.

HAWLEY TAKES AIM AT 'CORPORATE WELFARE' AFTER GOP-BACKED TAX BREAK BOOSTED CONTROVERSIAL INDUSTRY

"What we're saying is that we can do much better," said Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md. "Is it a little step forward? Yes. But it's not meeting the moment. So our view is we should expand it to make sure that ratepayers aren't having to subsidize the richest corporations on the planet."

But a lot of Republicans aren’t buying what Schumer and Van Hollen are saying. The Democratic objections are all about three things: Politics. An endangered GOP senator in the most expensive Senate contest in the country. And, Democrats are hoping to flip the seat in their favor.

"Sen. Schumer, what he cares about is the midterm election and politics. And I don't think he cares about the substance of this," said Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas. "Obviously there's a hot and heavy Senate race going on in Ohio, and he doesn't want to let Sen. Husted have something he can talk about when he goes home."

Republicans view the opportunity to turn the affordability issue against Democrats – capitalizing on Schumer’s remark and forcing Democrats to take a stand. Either you’re for affordability (especially as it pertains to the toxic issue of data centers) or you’re not. Moreover, this could boost Husted in his competitive contest with former Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio. In fact, it was the Senate GOP’s campaign arm which specifically flagged vulnerabilities for Republicans generally and Husted in particular over the summer.

Thune tees up a test vote on Wednesday to dare Democrats to either start debate on the bill or block it again. That vote requires 60 yeas. So Democratic cooperation is required. Although there’s skepticism anything happens, some Democrats may vote for it. That means the Senate is on the bill. And it’s open to debate and amendments. Thune would have to forge a bipartisan time agreement to finish the measure quickly.

Otherwise – by the book – this would drag into the weekend. And no one wants that. Especially Republicans with competitive races.

12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK

Thune and Schumer want senators back home campaigning. If Democrats impede the legislation Wednesday, the Senate might hang around Thursday or that’s it until after the midterms. Regardless, Republicans will have engineered a vote which they can boomerang against Democrats. Or, at least help Husted and send him back to the Buckeye State with a win.

While it’s not the best optic for Democrats to oppose this bill, their resistance might not directly wound anyone this fall. The reason: Democrats have a lot of chances to pick up seats. But vulnerable Democrats aren’t on the ballot. None of the Democratic Senate nominees in competitive seats like Maine, Florida, North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, Kansas and Alaska currently hold office. The only sitting Democrat in the cycle who has a mild race is Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va.

So for the Democrats, this is about playing defense. For Republicans, this is about playing offense. And the GOP is on offense primarily for Husted.

But the willingness of Senate GOPers to spend an extra week in Washington speaks volumes. It underscores how worried they are about the affordability issue. And in particular, their concern about elevating the work of Husted.

item.title: WATCH: ‘American Idol’ alum Caleb Flynn tells cops flag-carrying stranger came to door before wife’s shooting
item.description: Caleb Flynn's recorded police interview reveals what he told investigators happened the night Ashley Flynn was fatally shot in their Tipp City home.
item.content:encoded:
Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn's words took center stage Monday as his Ohio murder trial resumes for a second week, with jurors watching more of his recorded interview with police as prosecutors move closer to wrapping their case.

Jurors began watching the interview Friday, hearing Flynn describe what he said happened inside his Tipp City home before and after his wife, Ashley Flynn, was fatally shot Feb. 16.

Prosecutors allege Flynn shot Ashley in the back of the head and staged the scene to look like an intruder had broken in. He has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges.

DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER

Prosecutors also could call the couple's 10- and 12-year-old daughters, who were inside the home when their mother was killed, to testify Monday, though a final decision had not been made as court prepared to resume.

If called, the girls would testify by audio only, per the court.

In the interview played Monday, Flynn directed investigators to a stranger he said appeared outside the family’s home the day before Ashley was killed.

Flynn said Ashley and their daughters were in the living room when a car pulled up and sat outside before a man got out and walked to the front porch.

"My daughter can confirm," Flynn told investigators.

WATCH: Caleb Flynn tells police about ‘weird’ visitor at home day before wife’s killing

He described the man as having long hair and behaving awkwardly, with no company logo visible on his clothing. He said the man gave Ashley what he described as a "weird" sales pitch involving an American flag.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

He told the investigator Ashley eventually closed the door after the man indicated he would return later.

Flynn also walked investigators through his movements before the shooting, saying the family dogs were with him while he slept on the couch before one began shaking and scratching, waking him.

Flynn said he went to check on his daughters, retucked his youngest into bed and decided to lie down beside her.

He told investigators he was awakened again by gunshots.

MISTRESS SAYS SHE GAVE ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT ULTIMATUM BEFORE WIFE’S KILLING BLEW UP AFFAIR

"The shots woke you up?" an investigator asked.

"Yes, sir," Flynn responded, describing the shots as "back-to-back" and "loud."

Detective Sgt. Mike Morgan later testified that Flynn said he froze for four to six seconds before running across the house to the master bedroom, where he discovered Ashley had been shot.

The interview comes after jurors spent two days hearing from Flynn’s former mistress, Alleigha Botner, who detailed their affair and read messages exchanged in the months before Ashley’s death.

WATCH: 'You have murdered my heart': Secret affair messages revealed in Caleb Flynn trial

Botner testified Flynn repeatedly talked about wanting his wife dead, including one message in which he allegedly said he stayed up until 4 a.m. "literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

But Flynn’s attorneys used their cross-examination to emphasize the broader context of more than 107,000 messages exchanged during the roughly year-and-a-half affair, including emotionally charged language used by Botner herself.

Botner also testified she understood Flynn’s plans for Feb. 16 to mean he intended to finally leave Ashley and seek a divorce – not kill her.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Shortly after midnight that morning, however, Flynn allegedly told Botner, "It’s happening," followed by, "February 16th – day I’ll never forget."

SEND US A TIP

"You’re about to be free," Botner responded.

GOT A TIP?

"I choose you," Flynn replied.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Investigators have not recovered the gun prosecutors allege was used to kill Ashley despite extensive searches. There was no eyewitness to the shooting, and testimony showed no gunshot residue was found on Flynn.

Prosecutors have several additional witnesses they plan to call as they move closer to resting their case. It remained unclear Monday morning whether Flynn's daughters would be among them.

Fox News Digital has remained in contact with Flynn’s attorney, who declined to comment while the trial is ongoing.

item.title: Blue city funds immigrant activist program with taxpayer dollars, critics say it 'shuts citizens out'
item.description: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu's office offers $575 taxpayer-funded scholarships training immigrants in civic engagement and community organizing.
item.content:encoded:
Boston Mayor Michelle Wu’s administration is offering taxpayer-funded scholarships for an activist program while limiting participation to immigrants, including non-U.S. citizens, a requirement that has drawn criticism online.

The Immigrants Lead Boston program, run by the Mayor’s Office for Immigrant Advancement, is designed for "emerging leaders" interested in advocating for Boston’s immigrant communities. Participants meet city officials and receive training aimed at helping them engage with local government and organize within their communities during the 10-week program.

Critics have seized on both the taxpayer funding and the eligibility requirements, arguing that U.S.-born residents are excluded from a city-backed leadership program whose participants can receive a $575 scholarship.

"That is not charity. That is a political pipeline built to shut citizens out of their own city," one user wrote on X.

BOSTON TO GIVE LGBTQ+ MIGRANTS VOUCHERS FOR YOGA, MEDITATION, ‘CREATIVE HEALING’

"Paying illegal immigrants to learn political organizing to protest against the country they're in," one person wrote on X.

"For starters it sounds like discrimination," posted a user.

"Michelle WU is a communist who probably wants a American version of China," a person wrote taking shots at the Boston mayor.

TRUMP'S JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUES NEW YORK, OTHER BLUE STATES OVER TUITION FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

"Is this legal," asked one user.

"Illegal aliens have broken our laws. Any assistance given them other than assistance to leave the country, simply rewards their unlawful behavior, encourages other unlawful behavior, and more illegals to follow their lead," one person posted.

Similar taxpayer-backed benefits for immigrants have surfaced in other Democratic-led states, particularly in higher education.

NEBRASKA ENDS IN-STATE TUITION BENEFITS FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS UNDER DOJ DEAL

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

New York, Connecticut and Vermont have offered in-state tuition or other financial benefits to immigrants in the country illegally, while Oregon and Washington have provided access to benefits such as state grants or student loans. California has also allowed qualifying students in the country illegally to apply for state financial aid.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mayor Wu’s office for comment.

item.title: UK airbase terror suspects being released on bail as Iran denies connection
item.description: Five RAF Fairford terror suspects were released on bail as counter terrorism policing probes possible foreign state involvement in the plot.
item.content:encoded:
United Kingdom police are releasing five terror suspects on bail Monday after they were arrested on suspicion of a terror plot targeting a U.S. air base in Britain this weekend.

Laurence ​Taylor, head of ​Counter Terrorism Policing, confirmed that investigations into the five men are ongoing, "including ⁠that this may be actively committed ​by proxies ​or ⁠individuals either knowingly or unknowingly working on ⁠behalf ​of a ​foreign state." Meanwhile, the Iranian Embassy in the U.K. has denied any connection to the five men.

The Sunday night arrests came after a local resident and farmer in Gloucestershire told the BBC that she had called police late in the evening after coming across three white vans blocking a road near RAF Fairford air base. As she turned her car around, she told the BBC that her headlights illuminated a group of "hooded and masked men" who "panicked" upon being spotted and scrambled into a nearby woods.

IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE

Authorities identified the five men as "U.K. nationals," but did not offer any further details.

RAF Fairford plays host to significant U.S. Air Force assets and has been used as a launching point for multiple U.S. operations in the war against Iran in recent months.

US MILITARY RELEASES FOOTAGE OF MASSIVE OPERATION TO RESCUE INJURED AIRMAN STRANDED INSIDE IRAN

Defense Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed that the local farmer had at least a "partial picture" of the incident.

"I do want to thank the member of the public who acted quickly and called this in," Streeting told the BBC.

"I would also just say, respectfully, that she has a partial picture. And I won't go beyond that, in terms of commenting on operational security matters," he added.

The local, who asked to remain anonymous, told the BBC that she was astounded it had been her 999 call that "foiled whatever plans they had," adding that she was surprised the base didn't have more significant surveillance and security.

Iran's Embassy vehemently denied any connection with the incident in a public statement on Monday.

WALTZ CALLS OUT IRANIAN DIPLOMAT AT UN FOLLOWING DRONE STRIKES ON BAHRAIN AND KUWAIT

"The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in London categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran to arrest of five suspects in the vicinity of RAF Fairford base," the Embassy wrote on X.

"The Circulation of such fabricated speculations, particularly in the aftermath of the criminal acts of aggression committed by the United States and the Israeli regime against the Iranian people, will serve no purpose other than to fuel Iranophobia propaganda in the U.K.," the statement continued.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran reserves the right to take appropriate legal measures, as necessary, to safeguard the rights and interests of the country and its people in response to misleading and damaging media narratives," it added.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Americans win Presidents Cup on depth, Scheffler's complicated Sunday, and an overwhelming sense of false hope
item.description: Scottie Scheffler's classy putt concession and testy NBC interview defined a dramatic Sunday as the U.S. narrowly avoided Presidents Cup disaster.
item.content:encoded:
The final tally from the 2026 Presidents Cup read 17-13 in favor of the Americans, and while the U.S. team was able to avoid embarrassment against an inferior International side, you are lying to yourself if you came away from those four days of golf at Medinah feeling optimistic or overly impressed about United States team golf.

The Americans were thoroughly outplayed and outclassed for three consecutive days by the International side, but when Sunday singles rolled around, and it was 12 vs. 12, mano-a-mano, the U.S. was able to do something the International team could not: rely on depth. The average World Ranking for the U.S. team was 15.1 while the International's average was 50.1, and that differential showed when it mattered most.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

The Internationals carried a full three-point advantage into Sunday's session, needing just five of a possible 12 points to secure their second Presidents Cup victory ever, but ultimately earned only 2.5 points on the final day. If you turn it around, the Internationals lost 9.5 points of an available 12, which is tough to comprehend.

TEAM USA CAPTAIN THANKS TRUMP AFTER MASSIVE PRESIDENTS CUP COMEBACK: ‘HE GETS ALL THE CREDIT’

And yes, even with the Americans having the deeper stable of players and having the advantage of playing on home soil, it's perfectly okay to say that the International side choked away the event.

Ryo Hisatsune was 1-up thru five holes over Cameron Young before losing 3&2. Hideki Matsuyama was 1-up on Collin Morikawa with just four holes to play and couldn't even salvage a half point. Si Woo Kim and Jackson Koivun were all square standing on the 13th tee, and the American rookie who hasn't even been a professional golfer for 90 days at this point went on to earn a 2-up victory. Min Woo Lee was 1-up on Jacob Bridgeman thru 15 holes, blinked, and the American was standing over the Cup-clinching putt on the 18th to win the match 1-up.

GOLF STAR TOM KIM GOING FROM PRESIDENTS CUP TO ASIAN GAMES SEEKING EXEMPTION FROM MILITARY SERVICE

Golf is a fickle game, and while the putters collectively warmed up for the Americans down the stretch, it's fair to say that the Internationals bailed the U.S. out down the stretch. There was a sense of relief on the American side instead of accomplishment, which is noteworthy given that the U.S. entered the final day trailing by three points.

Chris Gotterup earning three points as a rookie, Koivun earning 2.5 points while shouldering the pressures of being the next great American player, and the six captain's picks going 6-0 in singles were clear bright spots for the Americans.

Credit is due on those fronts, but it was anything but a clean week for the U.S., both inside the ropes from players and outside the ropes operationally, which was the top objective with the 2027 Ryder Cup across the pond approaching. More on that later.

Scottie Scheffler did exactly what was expected of him on Sunday by earning a full point for the U.S. with a 2&1 victory over Nico Echavarria. While the result of the match was never in question, that isn't to say there wasn't any drama involving the World No. 1.

US PRESIDENTS CUP PLAYERS EXPLAIN HOW CHRISTIAN FAITH BUILDS FRIENDSHIPS AND PUTS GOLF IN PERSPECTIVE

On the 14th hole, a fan yelled during Echavarria's backswing as he hit his tee shot on the Par 4. Scheffler immediately reprimanded the fan, but then went above and beyond when the match made its way onto the green.

Already in for par on the hole, Scheffler conceded a 32-foot par putt to Echavarria. While the gesture was already classy, it also came at a moment where, if Echavarria had missed the lengthy par putt, the match would have gone to dormie, with Scheffler taking a 4-up lead into the final four holes. Instead, the concession extended the match a bit longer before Scheffler closed things out on the 17th hole.

While that was one of the more professional and classy acts we'll ever see on the golf course, the same couldn't be said for Scheffler's post-match interview with NBC's Cara Banks.

Scheffler did not play in the afternoon foursomes session on Saturday, which understandably made headlines. Sitting the No. 1 player in the world with your team trailing by three points was a very bold move from U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker, and one that deserves questions, but Scheffler was in no mood to provide answers.

When asked following his match on Sunday about being sat on Saturday, Scheffler didn't opt to give a generic, media-friendly answer, but instead he put the question back on Banks, asking her if she wanted to talk about Sunday's match.

Scheffler seems like the consummate professional and a genuinely good person – hell, he showed that on Sunday conceding the putt to Echavarria – but his exchange with Banks made no sense. He has had his moments with the media this season where he's made it clear that he doesn't have the time to answer what he sees as dumb questions, but Banks' question was the question of the weekend.

Nobody wants to hear Scheffler talk about beating the No. 61 player in the world on Sunday when the only exciting thing that happened in the match was a fan shouting in a backswing. The golf world does, however, want to know details around the No. 1 player in the world not playing in all five sessions in an event his team was, at the time, being embarrassed in.

Nobody is perfect, and Scheffler is just a human despite his freakish abilities with a golf club in his hand, but the old adage of sometimes you have to do things you don't enjoy applies here. At the end of the day, Scheffler getting testy with Banks for five seconds is going to be forgotten and has zero effect on his actual job of playing golf, but that doesn't mean we can't call it as we see it, which is simply ridiculous.

item.title: DHS tears into MS NOW after host touts ‘anti-authoritarian’ ICE monitoring group
item.description: DHS slammed MS NOW for featuring activists who train "ICE Watch" volunteers and are now turning their organizing efforts toward the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) fired back at MS NOW on Sunday after "Connect with Jacob Soboroff" host Jacob Soboroff highlighted an activist group that trains "ICE Watch" volunteers to monitor federal immigration operations and is now turning some of that organizing toward the midterm elections.

During Saturday's edition of the show, Soboroff discussed reporting about activists who previously monitored U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations and are now turning their attention toward election-related activity. MS NOW's description of the episode said, "ICE watchers once alerted neighbors about the presence of federal agents, now they are protecting the polls."

Soboroff’s segment featured Zachary Mueller, a senior strategist for the nonprofit States at the Core and referenced reporting from the outlet "The Intercept" about activists preparing to monitor polling locations.

States at the Core has described its work as opposing what it views as authoritarianism and has advertised trainings on both ICE monitoring and election protection.

NEW YORK TIMES TORCHED FOR ‘FALSE’ REPORTING ON ICE INVESTIGATIONS, OUTLET FIRES BACK

DHS pointed to attacks and threats against immigration officers while arguing that tools used to track federal agents could endanger law enforcement personnel and interfere with operations.

"Shame on MS NOW for promoting efforts to undermine those who keep our communities and streets safe from illegal alien crime," a DHS spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "ICE tracking apps put the lives of the men and women of law enforcement in danger as they go after terrorists, vicious gangs and violent criminal rings.

"Our law officers are facing an over 1,600% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats. Further, these apps are a method to interfere with law enforcement activities and harbor illegal aliens."

States at the Core said in March that tens of thousands of Americans had attended its ICE Watch training before it launched a program called "Beyond ICE Watch," which sought to expand neighborhood organizing beyond monitoring immigration enforcement.

SEVEN NONCITIZENS CHARGED IN NORTH TEXAS ELECTION-INTEGRITY INVESTIGATION

The organization described its mission in that announcement.

"Our mission is pretty simple. Help everyday people fight authoritarianism; help people fight for their freedoms," States at the Core said.

In September, the group advertised a training that sought to adapt ICE Watch techniques for the midterm elections, including documenting activity around communities and elections.

DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

States at the Core had previously drawn scrutiny for its ICE-monitoring tactics. In February, co-founder Jill Garvey trained "rapid responders" to use the military-derived "SALUTE" observation method — an acronym for size, activity, location, uniform, time and equipment — when documenting federal immigration personnel.

The FBI was also investigating alleged Signal groups used by anti-ICE activists to track, identify and potentially impede federal law enforcement officers. FBI Director Kash Patel said investigations would examine whether the alleged coordination crossed the line into violations of federal law.

DHS has reported a sharp increase in assaults against ICE personnel. The department said 647 assaults occurred between Jan. 20, 2025, and Sept. 20, 2026, compared with 37 during the corresponding period under the Biden administration, representing a 1,649% increase.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

DHS told Fox News Digital that it viewed messaging that encourages resistance to immigration enforcement as dangerous.

"Glorifying resistance to lawful immigration enforcement is irresponsible and dismissive of the victims and families who have suffered because of crimes committed by criminal illegal aliens," the spokesperson said. "Assaulting and obstructing ICE law enforcement is a crime and felony. Anyone who assaults law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law."

Fox News Digital reached out to States at the Core for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Republicans zero in on key player accused of helping Democrat fundraising giant hide foreign cash
item.description: House Republicans summon ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview, citing contradictions in his prior statements on donor verification.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: House Republicans' investigation into Democrats' main fundraising platform is heating up on the heels of an explosive report that raised questions about whether left-wing candidates' campaigns were raking in foreign cash.

Top House GOP committee chairs are summoning ActBlue attorney Ronald Machen for a closed-door interview sometime before Oct. 9, Fox News Digital has learned. A letter sent to Machen Monday morning stated that information he previously disclosed to investigators appears to contradict other data that has been collected, specifically on ActBlue's verification standards for making sure a donor is a U.S. citizen.

"On September 11, 2026, you provided a briefing to the House Administration, Judiciary, and Oversight and Government Reform Committees regarding the accuracy of ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones’s prior statements to Congress about ActBlue’s donor and passport collection processes," the letter said.

"Your review appears to be nothing more than an after-the-fact sugarcoating of ActBlue’s misconduct and Ms. Wallace-Jones’s misrepresentations to the House Administration Committee."

ANOTHER ACTBLUE LEADER PLEADS FIFTH AS HOUSE INVESTIGATES ALLEGED FOREIGN DONATIONS

The letter was sent by House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., and House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., who lead the panels probing ActBlue.

ACTBLUE CO-FOUNDER PLEADS FIFTH AMENDMENT IN CLOSED-DOOR HOUSE GOP GRILLING

ActBlue is a massive platform for campaigns to raise money that's used by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and the Democratic leaders of the House and Senate, among others.

Republican lawmakers have long accused the company of having lax verification standards for donors, something ActBlue has said it actively improved since the start of the GOP's probe. But a new report released earlier this month, first reported by Fox News Digital, appears to show employees green-lighting donations despite some questions about where they came from.

FAR-LEFT POLITICIANS STILL USING ACTBLUE AS 88-YEAR-OLD DISPUTES DONATING NEARLY $150,000 TO FUNDRAISING GIANT

Chief among the GOP's concerns is ActBlue's passport number verification. According to the report, the field only requires the correct number of characters for a U.S. passport number rather than a valid code for a donation to be accepted.

The Monday letter also points to a 2024 "contemporaneous review by ActBlue’s then-outside counsel, former Biden White House Counsel Dana Remus" which allegedly found "'a substantial risk that some of the funds' raised for Democrat campaigns and causes by ActBlue 'were impermissible contributions from foreign nationals.'"

Remus' review further found that "passport checks did not always happen" and were "never conducted" when donations were made using third-party fiscal platforms like Apple Pay or PayPal, the letter said.

The Republican chairs said Machen's prior comments to Congress "conceded that your 'forensic' review found that ActBlue processed and accepted donations with foreign indicators even though ActBlue failed to identify a 'passport number' or 'other indicia of eligibility' for the donor.

HOUSE DEM LASHES OUT AT GOP EFFORTS TO PROBE FOREIGN DONATIONS WITH STUNNING CLAIM ON MOTIVE

"Nonetheless, you defended Ms. Wallace-Jones’s representations to Congress by arguing that ActBlue’s compliance and vetting policy was 'as close to 100 percent as it could be,'" the letter said.

"Documents produced to the Committees undercut your assertion. These documents demonstrate that if a donor did not have a U.S. passport or a U.S. address, an ActBlue employee retained the ability to determine an 'alternative method of verifying the [donor’s] citizenship.' This means an ActBlue employee could put 'a placeholder,' including 'ACTBLUEXX,' 'in the passport number field of [the donor’s] ActBlue account.' The placeholder allows ActBlue to accept all subsequent contributions from the donor without requiring a U.S. passport number."

ACTBLUE SCRUTINY FUELS NEW GOP BILLS TO TIGHTEN ELECTION DONATION RULES

The letter said Machen's review was also limited to 2023, arguing it left out potentially valuable information about 2024.

"As such, the review did not accurately represent the totality of ActBlue’s foreign donation vetting and donor outreach practices during the 2024 election cycle. In fact, documents produced to the Committees show that ActBlue relaxed its vetting practices twice in 2024—data that your narrow 'forensic' review did not capture," the letter said.

ACTBLUE SUES TEXAS AG KEN PAXTON, ALLEGING POLITICAL RETALIATION OVER DEMOCRATS' FUNDRAISING

It also charged that he disputed Remus' analysis without going into detail on how he established his own findings.

ActBlue has consistently denied any wrongdoing and dismissed Republicans' most recent findings in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"There’s nothing to see here. After we released findings of a third-party forensic analysis that completely undermined a central claim that they have made against ActBlue, Republicans are refusing to move on," ActBlue said. "Instead, they are orchestrating another political stunt before rushing out of town weeks early to go campaign. This coordinated campaign against ActBlue isn’t about the facts, or legislating, it’s about Republicans’ efforts to silence organizations they believe threaten their agenda."

A closed-door interview summons is not the same as a subpoena, which is a legally binding order.

item.title: Largest-ever US steel plant is coming to a key red state as Trump unveils $15B investment
item.description: Trump announces Mesabi Metallics' $15 billion Iowa steel plant, but the massive facility won't produce its first steel until 2030 at the earliest.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is unveiling Monday plans for a massive steel plant in Iowa that the White House says will be the largest in American history and promises to bring 1,750 permanent jobs to the state.

The roughly $15 billion steel plant is touted as a major new investment and evidence that Trump's economic agenda is bringing heavy manufacturing back to the U.S. with just over a month until the midterms. It will create between 5,000 and 6,000 construction jobs during its first phase.

Trump is expected to make the announcement from the Oval Office at 2 p.m. alongside executives from Mesabi Metallics, a White House official told Fox News Digital. The company plans to build the facility using iron ore from its newly constructed mine in Minnesota.

SEN KEVIN CRAMER: CHINA BUILDS FOR WAR WHILE AMERICA WAITS ON PERMITS

The Iowa plant is expected to produce 7.5 million tons of steel annually in its first phase before eventually reaching 10 million tons per year, according to the White House. The administration says that would make it the largest steel plant ever built in the U.S.

If completed as planned, the project would represent a significant expansion of American steel-making capacity. At its planned 10 million tons of annual production, the Iowa plant alone would have output equivalent to roughly one-tenth of what the entire U.S. steel industry produced last year.

The project would also create a fully domestic supply chain, according to the White House, using iron ore mined at Mesabi's Minnesota operation to produce finished steel in Iowa.

But the scale of Monday's announcement also comes with a long timeline: Mesabi does not expect the Iowa facility to produce its first steel until 2030.

Trump has frequently highlighted large investment commitments as evidence that his tariffs and other economic policies are encouraging companies to build in the United States rather than invest abroad. The administration has announced hundreds of billions of dollars in planned investments from foreign governments and corporations, many of which are designed to unfold over several years.

Mesabi's Minnesota operation also illustrates the challenges that can accompany large industrial projects. The project traces back nearly two decades and encountered years of financing problems and missed deadlines before Essar Steel Minnesota filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016. It later emerged from bankruptcy as Mesabi Metallics, and Essar eventually regained control.

The project has since made substantial progress. Mesabi has begun mining and commissioning work at the Minnesota operation, although commercial pellet production has not yet begun. A recent SEC filing by a company that holds a royalty interest in the project said initial DR-grade pellet production is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by an eight- to 12-month ramp-up to commercial production.

The White House says the Minnesota operation will ultimately produce 7.5 million tons annually and create roughly 350 permanent jobs.

The administration is also emphasizing the national security implications of the Iowa project. The new plant will be capable of producing high-grade steel used to meet defense-sector requirements, according to the White House, as Washington seeks to strengthen domestic supply chains for materials used by the military and critical infrastructure.

"President Trump is delivering on his promise to rebuild American industry, reshore manufacturing, and create new jobs," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers told Fox News Digital.

"Today’s announcement underscores the President’s historic efforts to revitalize the U.S. steel industry—supporting local communities, strengthening supply chains, and protecting our national security," Rogers said. "After decades of decline, this President is restoring America’s industrial competitiveness and securing trillions of dollars in new investment."

The announcement comes as Trump points to tariffs as a tool for encouraging companies to manufacture in the United States. Trump doubled tariffs on steel and aluminum imports to 50% last year, arguing that protecting domestic producers from cheaper foreign competition would rebuild an industry critical to the economy and national security.

TRUMP’S REINDUSTRIALIZATION AGENDA FACES ITS BIGGEST HURDLE — AMERICANS

The policy has also increased costs for companies that consume steel. S&P Global reported that federal data showed prices for iron and steel rose 10.4% between April 2025 and April 2026, while the steel mill products index climbed 13.3%, even as domestic steel production increased.

Unlike many newer U.S. steel facilities, which are smaller electric arc furnace plants, the Iowa project will be a large-scale integrated steel facility. The White House says it will be the first new "mega-steel" plant built in the United States since the 1960s.

The first phase of the steel plant and the Minnesota mine together represent nearly $18 billion in investment, according to the administration. The White House estimates the first phase will generate approximately $95 billion in economic activity during construction and the plant's first decade of operation.

Trump is expected to be joined for Monday's announcement by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, National Energy Dominance Council Executive Director Jarrod Agen and Export-Import Bank Chairman John Jovanovic, along with Mesabi Metallics Chairman Rewant Ruia, board member Prashant Ruia and CEO Joe Broking.

item.title: The next connected device could be the shirt you're wearing
item.description: ShareAScan turns T-shirts into scannable digital business cards with QR codes that link to profiles the owner can update anytime they choose.
item.content:encoded:
A T-shirt has always been able to tell you something about the person wearing it. Maybe it shows a favorite band, sports team or funny message. Now, it can potentially open an entire digital profile. That is the idea behind ShareAScan, a startup using QR code clothing to connect apparel and other physical products with digital content that can change over time.

Scan a code with your smartphone, and you can see whatever experience the owner has chosen to share. That might include text, photos, video, music, a portfolio, social content or information about a business. The shirt itself does not contain a battery, Bluetooth connection or hidden computer. The technology starts with a printed QR code and the web platform behind it. So, could the next connected device actually be something you wear?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

EMPTY ENVELOPES IN YOUR MAILBOX? DO NOT SCAN THAT CODE

The basic idea is simple. ShareAScan prints a unique QR code on products such as T-shirts, hoodies, hats, mugs and other merchandise. A person scans the code using the camera already built into a smartphone. No special scanning app is required.

However, the interesting part happens behind that code. Instead of permanently tying the printed QR code to one piece of content, ShareAScan lets the owner change what appears later. The physical code stays the same while the digital experience behind it changes. For example, someone could use a shirt to share a portfolio at a conference and later update the content to promote a project or event.

The company describes its technology as a patent-pending platform connecting physical products with dynamic, user-controlled digital identities. Its September announcement says a single product can become a changing introduction, portfolio, personal message or business card. That makes the concept more interesting than simply printing a website address across your chest.

ShareAScan was founded by sisters Shara and Kailey Zuckerman. Shara is a college student studying business, finance and artificial intelligence, while Kailey is still in high school. The company got a major dose of exposure this month when its QR merchandise was included in gift bags distributed around the 78th Emmy Awards. ShareAScan merchandise went into gift bags for nominees, presenters and performers. Still, the bigger story goes beyond an awards-show gift bag. It is another example of physical products gaining a digital layer that can change long after you buy them.

There are plenty of ways people could use this. A business owner could wear a shirt that introduces a company. A creator could share recent work. Someone at a conference could use it as a digital introduction. Meanwhile, a musician could share new content or an organization could promote an event. Because the material behind the QR code can change, the same physical product can serve different purposes over time.

ShareAScan says purchases start at $19 and current customers do not pay an ongoing subscription fee. The company also tells CyberGuy that customers who buy under the current model will not later face a subscription charge even if its terms change for future customers. That gives the physical product something most ordinary clothing never had before: content that can keep changing after you take it home.

ShareAScan tells CyberGuy that scans are anonymous. The company says it collects no information about the scanner unless an owner's access restrictions require it to check whether that scanner is allowed to view the content.

If someone does not have permission, the company says that person simply does not receive access. ShareAScan also says it does not currently give the wearer scan analytics. In other words, wearing one of these products does not give you a dashboard showing who walked by and scanned your code. The company says owners can choose who gets access to their content and can completely delete their account and associated data.

However, there is still another side to privacy: what you decide to reveal. If you make your full name, workplace, photos, social accounts or other personal information publicly available, someone who scans you may learn quite a bit. That is why anyone using connected clothing should look at the experience from a stranger's point of view before wearing it in public.

QR CODE EMAIL SCAM TARGETS EMPLOYEE REVIEWS

This required an important clarification from the company. ShareAScan tells CyberGuy that its QR codes cannot point directly to an outside website. Instead, scanning the code first opens the experience hosted through its platform. However, content within that experience can include links. The company says it scans uploads for malicious links, phishing links, pornography and other inappropriate material. It also says people review flagged material.

ShareAScan acknowledges that its screening cannot catch everything. That makes its setup different from a random QR sticker that directly sends your browser to an unknown website. Even so, you should never treat every QR code as automatically safe simply because scanning has become second nature.

The FTC continues to warn about criminals using QR codes to send people to fake websites designed to steal passwords, financial information and other personal data. In a fresh warning published Sept. 3, the agency again advised people to inspect the destination before opening a QR link. So, the familiar security advice still applies whenever you pick up your phone to scan something.

Connected clothing could naturally catch the attention of younger users, especially when it links fashion with social content. ShareAScan tells CyberGuy that account holders must be at least 18 years old.

At the same time, the company acknowledges that an age requirement cannot completely stop someone younger from trying to create an account. That makes conversations about public sharing especially important for families. A QR code someone wears outside can potentially expose information to people they have never met.

A scannable shirt also has to hold up to everyday wear. ShareAScan says its QR codes have been tested through repeated washing and continue to scan after normal use. Of course, a QR code still needs to remain physically readable. Heavy damage, fading or distortion could eventually interfere with any printed code.

There is another longevity issue too. Unlike a normal graphic on a shirt, this feature depends on the online platform behind it. ShareAScan says it plans to keep the platform operating and has purchased insurance intended to help support continued operation. That is worth keeping in mind with any connected product that depends on a company's servers long after the initial purchase.

QR codes are already everywhere, from tickets and restaurant tables to payment screens and packages. Now, they are starting to show up on the things we wear. ShareAScan takes that familiar technology and gives it a more personal use. Instead of linking to one fixed piece of information, the code can connect to content that the owner changes over time.

That means a sweatshirt could introduce your business at a conference, while a T-shirt could share your latest project, interests or something you simply want people to know about you. A quick scan could even become an easy way to start a conversation. But once your clothing can share information about you, it is worth thinking about exactly what you are putting out there. Anything you make public could potentially be seen by someone you have never met.

AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU

If clothing is going to become scannable, a few simple precautions can help you share without giving away too much.

Start with your public profile. Look at exactly what appears to someone who does not know you. Avoid exposing your home address, private phone number, personal email or other sensitive information.

Review who can access your content. ShareAScan says owners can limit access, so use those controls when you want to share something with a smaller group.

Create content specifically for public sharing. That can help you avoid giving strangers access to personal accounts filled with years of photos, posts or identifying information.

Treat QR codes like links. ShareAScan says it screens content on its platform, but QR codes in general can still lead to trouble. If anything asks for a password, payment information or other sensitive data unexpectedly, stop.

Look at the address your phone shows before opening a QR link. The FTC recommends checking for misspellings and switched letters that can signal an impersonation site.

Install and keep strong antivirus software active on your devices. It can help detect malicious links, phishing pages, dangerous downloads and other threats you may encounter after scanning a QR code. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com. Also, keep your phone's built-in security protections and software updates turned on too. No security tool can make every QR code safe, so always check where a code is taking you before entering passwords, payment information or other sensitive data.

What I like about this idea is how simple it is. There is no battery, Bluetooth or complicated hardware inside the shirt. The QR code does the work, and the person wearing it can keep changing what people see after they scan. ShareAScan also says it has built in some useful controls. Scans are anonymous, owners can limit who sees their content and the code itself does not send you straight to an outside website. The company also says it checks uploaded content for malicious material. The bigger question is how much of yourself you want to make scannable. If your shirt becomes part of your digital identity, take a minute to look at exactly what a stranger could learn about you before you wear it out the door.

Would you wear a shirt that could turn a quick QR scan into a new connection? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

item.title: WWE strikes intriguing content partnership as pro wrestling's popularity continues to soar
item.description: WWE's new Bleacher Report deal grants global highlight rights across "Raw," "SmackDown" and premium live events amid Warner Bros. Discovery shifts.
item.content:encoded:
WWE announced a strategic content partnership with Bleacher Report on Monday.

Bleacher Report will have the global rights to highlights across WWE’s programming, including "Monday Night Raw," "Friday Night SmackDown," NXT and premium live events, the company said in a news release. Bleacher Report will also have a presence at certain WWE premium live events.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

"Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture," WWE executive vice president Alex Varga said in a statement. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE’s commitment to bringing our content to a global audience."

Bleacher Report general manager Bennett Spector added, "WWE fans don’t just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That’s exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for.

"This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations."

On the surface, the partnership appeared to be just another way for WWE to further its global reach across social media.

WWE boasts more than 102 million followers on Facebook, 40.1 million followers on TikTok, 35 million followers on Instagram and 13 million followers on X. But the deal comes days after Paramount reached a settlement with states that sued to block the Warner Bros. Discovery takeover.

But it’s worth noting that Bleacher Report is a subsidiary of Warner Bros. Discovery through TNT Sports. WWE’s U.S. competitor All Elite Wrestling (AEW), which is owned by Tony Khan, airs its weekly shows on TNT, TBS and HBO Max. Speculation aside, the WWE and Bleacher Report agreement is striking at a time when interest in pro wrestling – no matter the promotion – is at an all-time high.

Warner Bros. Discovery announced in June 2025 it planned to keep TNT Sports and Bleacher Report under Global Networks, separating it form its TV and film endeavors. Sportico reported in December that was still the plan for the end of 2026.

Bleacher Report previously hosted AEW pay-per-views on its streaming platform before discontinuing it in 2024.

Khan has repeatedly welcomed the merger and reiterated his happiness after All Out over the weekend.

"I think this is exciting because we grew in a situation where the new corporate leadership in 2022, at that time, over four years ago, was something of an unknown entity to us and we really won them over immediately," he said, via Fightful. "It’s something I take a lot of pride in. We’ve been through several different regimes here. When AEW launched, AT&T was still in charge and then it’s been a lot of change with Discovery coming in. There was a period of transition there during 2020, 2021, where a lot of changes were made before Discovery took over in 2022 and they’ve made a lot of changes over the years and for AEW, there have been changes for the better, clearly, as we’ve grown the company and expanded.

"Now, we enter something that I consider more of a known quantity and I’m very excited about it. I think we’ve proven that AEW is a feather in the cap of a media company that we are a great partner, and for me, I’ll work to make sure that AEW fits in any corporate structure. I’ll work very hard, and I think I’ve proven time after time that I am the ultimate corporate soldier, and that is why AEW continues to grow and expand as the media landscape changes and I think that’s why Warner Bros., even as the company has evolved and changed, AEW has always been a very important part of the portfolio for years and years and I expect that’s gonna continue with AEW and Warner Bros. for many years to come."
